Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — Restart path now only kills when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, but SpawnProcess is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process (MRO is SpawnProcess -> BaseProcess, verified), so a hung flusher is never killed; a second process is spawned on the same shards, both flush and produce the same segments (duplicates), both write the same shared healthy_since/backpressure_since Values (so a zombie can mask or clear health/backpressure state), and up to 11 zombies with Kafka producers pile up per index (the old code called kill() unconditionally)

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — join() `break`s out once the deadline passes, so the remaining processes are never waited on or terminated, and the `isinstance(..., multiprocessing.Process)` guard at :346 is never true for SpawnProcess, so no flusher process is ever terminated; on a rebalance, hung processes keep running next to the new SpanFlusher's processes on the same shards

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:51 — max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means the factory default (None) and `--flusher-processes 0` both silently spawn one full Sentry process per assigned partition (which is also what the docstring says), while the CLI says it defaults to 1; nothing validates the value (no IntRange(min=1))

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as falsy, so `--flusher-processes 0` will silently fall back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and potentially spawn one process per shard. The new Click option uses `type=int` with no range/validation, so `0` is allowed and triggers this behavior. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral defect (surprising and potentially resource-explosive) caused by the `or` fallback and missing `IntRange(min=1)`/explicit validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:66 — A negative --flusher-processes gives num_processes=-1, so range(-1) makes the map empty and `i % -1 == 0` then raises a confusing KeyError at startup instead of a clear CLI validation error

adjudication.rationale: The new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is defined as `type=int` with no validation, so a negative value can reach `SpanFlusher.__init__` as `max_processes`. The code then does `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (so `-1` is kept), `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` (becomes `-1`), builds `process_to_shards_map` with `range(self.num_processes)` (empty), and then computes `process_index = i % self.num_processes` (0) and tries to append into `self.process_to_shards_map[0]`, causing a startup KeyError instead of a clear CLI validation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:299 — submit() now calls get_memory_info()/record_stored_segments() once per per-process buffer; get_memory_info returns memory usage for the whole Redis cluster (not per shard), so each submit sends N times the INFO scans to the same nodes and counts the same memory N times over (the ratio only stays correct by accident)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SpanFlusher.submit()` was changed to iterate over `self.buffers.values()` and call `buffer.record_stored_segments()` for each per-process buffer, and to build `memory_infos` by calling `buffer.get_memory_info()` for each buffer and concatenating the results before summing `used`/`available` (see the new loops in `submit()`). This undeniably increases the number of `get_memory_info()` invocations per submit from 1 to N (number of flusher processes/buffers), which could duplicate expensive Redis INFO/memory queries and duplicate-count the same cluster-wide totals if `get_memory_info()` is not shard-scoped. The claim that `get_memory_info()` is cluster-wide is not verifiable from this diff alone, so this is best treated as a performance/architecture concern introduced by the change rather than a provable correctness bug.

The test never drives any flush work (no segments/spans written to Redis and flushed), and it does not exercise the new multi-process health/restart/backpressure paths added in `SpanFlusher` (`_ensure_processes_alive`, per-process `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, killing/recreating processes). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — Hung flusher is never killed on restart because spawn-context SpawnProcess is not an instance of multiprocessing.Process (the old code called kill() unconditionally), so a second process gets started on the same shards and the old one is orphaned while still sharing the healthy/backpressure Values, which can produce duplicate segments

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, the restart path only calls `kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is true. But processes are created via `self.mp_context.Process` where `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so the concrete type is a spawn-context `SpawnProcess`. On platforms where the default `multiprocessing.Process` is not the spawn-context class (e.g. default fork on many Unix setups), this `isinstance` check can fail, meaning a hung-but-alive process won’t be killed before `_create_process_for_shards(...)` starts a replacement for the same shard set. Since the per-process `Value`s (`process_healthy_since[...]`, `process_backpressure_since[...]`) are reused across restarts, the old and new workers can run concurrently and act on the same shards, plausibly causing duplicate flush/produce behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — join() breaks out of the loop once the deadline passes, so the remaining flusher processes are never waited on or terminated; the terminate() guard also never matches SpawnProcess, so processes outlive join and keep flushing old shards across rebalances

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the loop over self.processes breaks entirely when the deadline is exceeded (`if remaining_time <= 0: break`), so any remaining flusher processes after the current index are neither waited on nor terminated (no further `process.terminate()` calls). This can leave orphaned flusher processes running past join() and continuing to flush. The claim that `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` never matches SpawnProcess is not verifiable from the diff and is likely incorrect, but the early `break` behavior is a concrete, diff-grounded shutdown bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:65 — Negative --flusher-processes is truthy, so num_processes becomes negative, process_to_shards_map ends up empty and `i % num_processes` gives a KeyError at construction; nothing validates the CLI value

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CLI option `--flusher-processes` (type=int) with no validation. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means a negative value (e.g. -1) is truthy and will be used. Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes negative, `range(self.num_processes)` yields an empty `process_to_shards_map`, and the subsequent loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`, which will KeyError because the map is empty. This is a real crash introduced by the new option handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:127 — _create_process_for_shard is never called, and the `if not process` check at line 222 can never be true (Process/Thread objects are always truthy)

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:62 — The added time.sleep(0.1) does nothing because the test monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op, so it doesn't give the flusher time and the drift-vs-stop race is still there

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — New `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard is always False for spawn-context `SpawnProcess` (subclass of BaseProcess, not multiprocessing.Process), so hung/dead flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned (same wrong check makes join()'s terminate() at :346 a no-op), leaking processes that keep flushing the same shards

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive()` and `join()`, the code gates `kill()`/`terminate()` behind `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. But flusher processes are created via `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `self.mp_context.Process`, producing `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances. On platforms where `multiprocessing.Process` refers to the *default* context’s `Process` class (often fork on Linux), a `SpawnProcess` is not an instance of `multiprocessing.Process`, so the guard can be false and the unhealthy process won’t be killed/terminated before a replacement is started, leaking processes for the same shards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:93 — SpanFlusher ignores the injected `buffer` (used only for `assigned_shards`) and builds its own `SpansBuffer(shards)` internally, creating a hidden dependency on the SpansBuffer constructor and silently dropping any configuration on the injected instance

adjudication.rationale: In the new `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the passed `buffer: SpansBuffer` is only used for `buffer.assigned_shards` to build `process_to_shards_map` and determine `num_processes/max_processes`. Each worker is then given a freshly constructed `SpansBuffer(shards)` in `_create_process_for_shards`, and later `submit()`/memory checks iterate over `self.buffers.values()` rather than using the injected instance. This is a real, diff-grounded design concern (the injected `buffer` is effectively not honored beyond shard listing and the class now depends on being able to reconstruct `SpansBuffer` from shard IDs), but the claim about “silently dropping any configuration on the injected instance” is not directly verifiable from the diff because we can’t see whether `SpansBuffer` carries additional configuration/state beyond shards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:199 — Inconsistent metric tag keys: `wait_produce` uses `shards` while `produce`/`segment_size_bytes` use `shard` (with a comma-joined string) and `flusher_unhealthy` (:244) uses `shard` with a single int, breaking dashboard queries and mixing value semantics under one key

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys/semantics in `SpanFlusher.main`: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use tag key `shard` with a comma-joined string of multiple shard ids, while `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses a different key (`shards`). This inconsistency is directly visible in the diff and would split/obscure metric series and break queries expecting consistent tag keys/values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:242 — spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is now incremented once per shard for a single process failure, so the metric's count silently inflates by shards-per-process vs. the old one-incr-per-event semantics

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a single process is unhealthy the code now does `for shard in shards: metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", ...)`, emitting one increment per shard handled by that process. Previously `_ensure_process_alive` emitted exactly one increment per unhealthy event (`metrics.incr(... tags={"cause": cause})`). This is a real, diff-grounded change in metric semantics that can inflate counts by shards-per-process and potentially affect dashboards/alerts, but it’s an observability/monitoring behavior change rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:127 — _create_process_for_shard` is dead code with no callers anywhere in src/ or tests/

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:222 — if not process: continue` is unreachable since `self.processes` only ever holds Process/Thread objects, which are always truthy

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, `self.processes` is populated only via `_create_process_for_shards`, which assigns a `multiprocessing.Process` or `threading.Thread` object to `self.processes[process_index]`. These objects are truthy, and the diff shows no path where `None`/falsy values are inserted, so `if not process: continue` is effectively redundant. However, this is not a correctness defect—just a minor cleanup/style point—so it doesn’t qualify as a bug or important non-bug issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:32 — Class docstring says "Creates one process per shard" but the code creates min(max_processes, len(shards)) processes with round-robin shard sharing

adjudication.rationale: The updated SpanFlusher docstring states: "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing." However, the implementation sets `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` and assigns shards round-robin via `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, meaning multiple shards can share a single process when `max_processes < len(assigned_shards)`. This is a documentation/behavior mismatch, not a functional defect in the logic shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:235 — Misleading comments: ":235 Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy" and ":178 Update healthy_since for all shards" describe per-shard tracking, but there is a single per-process healthy_since Value

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SpanFlusher` explicitly tracks health per *process* via `self.process_healthy_since[process_index] = mp_context.Value(...)` and passes that single `healthy_since` Value into each process’s `main(...)`. The comment at ~178 (“Update healthy_since for all shards handled by this process”) matches this design: one process may handle multiple shards, and the single per-process `healthy_since` is intended to represent the whole shard-group’s health. The comment at ~235 (“Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy”) is at worst slightly imprecise wording, but the finding frames it as a substantive tracking mismatch; the code never claims to track per-shard health, and the metric tagging per shard is derived from the process’s shard list. This is a minor comment/style nit, not a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:229 — getattr(process, "exitcode", "unknown")` on a `SpawnProcess | Thread` union is the exact getattr/hasattr-on-union pattern the same PR adds to CLAUDE.md as an anti-pattern; should branch with isinstance

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, `process` is a `SpawnProcess | threading.Thread` and the code uses `getattr(process, "exitcode", "unknown")` only when `not process.is_alive()`. This is safe for both union members (Threads simply lack `exitcode` so the default is used), and it does not match the PR’s documented anti-pattern (`hasattr()` on unions). Nothing in the diff shows this causes incorrect behavior; at most it’s a minor style/consistency preference, not a verifiable defect or important issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:256 — except (ValueError, AttributeError)` around kill(): AttributeError is only reachable because of the broken isinstance guard and just hides type-boundary mistakes

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the code attempts to kill unhealthy processes only when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is true. But processes are created via `self.mp_context.Process` from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, which yields a `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instance; that class is not necessarily an instance of `multiprocessing.Process` (it subclasses `BaseProcess` directly). As a result, the kill path may never run for real spawned processes (same issue in `join()` for `terminate()`), leaving hung processes alive while restarting, which is broken behavior. The `except (ValueError, AttributeError)` also risks masking misuse at this boundary rather than fixing the type/guard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:69 — Six parallel dicts keyed by process_index (processes, buffers, process_to_shards_map, process_healthy_since, process_backpressure_since, process_restarts) should be one per-process record/dataclass to avoid state drifting apart

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce multiple parallel per-process data structures keyed by `process_index` in `SpanFlusher.__init__` (e.g., `process_to_shards_map`, `processes`, `buffers`, `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`). This is a real maintainability/architecture concern created by the change: updates/restarts in `_create_process_for_shards` / `_ensure_processes_alive` must keep these dicts consistent, and the design makes it easier for state to diverge over time. However, the finding does not point to a concrete, verifiable correctness defect in the diff by itself—it's about risk/clarity rather than a demonstrated bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:41 — flusher_processes: int | None = None` means "all shards" in code while the CLI default is 1 and help text says "Defaults to 1"; with `max_processes or len(...)` (flusher.py:51) 0 also means "all shards", so there are two different defaults

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__` the line `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` makes `0` behave the same as `None` (i.e., “use all shards / as many processes as shards”). Given the new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is an `int` with help text “Maximum number of processes… Defaults to 1.”, passing `0` would unexpectedly create processes rather than limiting/disabled/erroring. Also, the factory default `flusher_processes: int | None = None` differs from the CLI default of `1`, creating inconsistent defaults between programmatic use (None => all shards) and CLI use (1). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:435 — --flusher-processes` uses `type=int` with no `click.IntRange(min=1)`, so a negative value gives num_processes<0 and fails with an unclear KeyError in the shard map instead of a CLI validation error

adjudication.rationale: The new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is defined as `type=int` with no minimum validation. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will keep a negative value (truthy), leading to `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` being negative. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:337 — In join(), `process_index` is unused and the `remaining_time` pre-check duplicates the deadline check in the inner while loop; the early `break` also skips terminate() for the remaining processes

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:300 — submit() calls get_memory_info() once per per-process buffer, but every buffer points at the same span-buffer Redis cluster (iter_cluster_memory_usage sends INFO to every node), so each submit sends N times as many INFO calls to every node and counts used/available N times; calling it once would do

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.submit(), the diff changes memory polling from a single `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` call to iterating over every per-process `SpansBuffer` (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:192 — The new `shard`/`shards` metric tags are the comma-joined list of all shards the process owns (e.g. "0,1,...,15" with the default of 1 process); the value changes with partition assignment and rebalances, so possible values grow combinatorially, and the tag is added to the per-segment segment_size_bytes distribution plus the produce/wait_produce timers (which also use different tag keys, `shard` vs `shards`, at 185/199)

This is verifiable in the diff and creates (1) inconsistent tag keys (`shard` vs `shards`) for related metrics and (2) potentially high-cardinality tag values since the comma-joined shard set can vary with partition assignment/rebalances and process-to-shards grouping. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:51 — max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means any caller that does not pass flusher_processes (the factory default is None, tests, or a value of 0) gets one spawned process per assigned partition, each doing a full Sentry import, and this happens again on every rebalance; that does not match the CLI default of 1 and is unbounded when one consumer is assigned many partitions

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:269 — record_stored_segments() now runs one Redis pipeline per per-process buffer, one after another, on every submit instead of a single pipeline covering all assigned shards, so ZCARD round trips per submit grow N times on the consumer's main thread

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.submit(), the diff changes from a single `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` call to iterating `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` (around the `submit` method). adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:346 — join() keeps the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard, which is a no-op for SpawnProcess, and now breaks out of the loop once the deadline passes, so on each rebalance none of the N old flusher processes is terminated; a hung one lingers alongside the N newly spawned ones

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` breaks entirely when `remaining_time <= 0` (deadline passed) before reaching later processes, and the `terminate()` call is inside the per-process loop. That means any processes not yet iterated are never terminated in this join call and could linger after a rebalance/shutdown with a timeout. The finding’s claim that `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is a no-op for SpawnProcess is not verifiable from the diff (SpawnProcess is typically a multiprocessing Process subtype), but the timeout/break behavior causing skipped termination is a real, diff-grounded defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — The hung-process kill is now guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, which is always False for `SpawnProcess` from the spawn context (verified: SpawnProcess subclasses BaseProcess, not context.Process), so hung flushers are never killed and keep running untracked alongside their replacement on the same shards and shared healthy_since/backpressure_since Values (regression from the old unconditional `kill()`), which leaks up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS orphans per slot and can double-flush segments if a hung process recovers

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the code only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` (and similarly only `terminate()` in `join()` under the same guard). But processes are created via `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `make_process = self.mp_context.Process`, so the concrete type will be the spawn-context process class (e.g. `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`). `multiprocessing.Process` refers to the *default* context’s Process class; on platforms where the default context is not spawn (commonly `fork` on Unix), a spawn-context process will not be an instance of `multiprocessing.Process`, so the kill/terminate path will be skipped. The diff also immediately recreates a replacement process for the same shards, meaning the old process can remain running untracked alongside the new one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — In join(), once the deadline passes the loop `break`s and skips the remaining processes, and the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` terminate guard at line 346 is also never true for SpawnProcess, so flushers that have not exited are never terminated; after a rebalance they keep running next to the N newly spawned flushers for the same Redis shards

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, when a `timeout` is provided and the computed `remaining_time <= 0`, the code does `break` out of the *entire* `for process_index, process in self.processes.items()` loop. That means any remaining flusher processes after the first one encountered will not be waited on or terminated (the `terminate()` call is inside the loop and won’t run for skipped processes). This is a concrete shutdown/cleanup correctness issue introduced by the new multi-process management in this diff. The finding’s additional claim about `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` never matching `SpawnProcess` is plausible but not strictly verifiable from the diff alone; however, the deadline `break` issue alone is sufficient to be a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:247 — Restart counters are per-process and lifetime-cumulative with no reset after a healthy period, so sporadic hangs in any one of N flushers eventually hit MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS and raise RuntimeError that takes down the whole consumer, and every "restart" of a hang leaks an unkilled process as described in the P1 finding

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes restart counts lifetime-cumulative per flusher process (`self.process_restarts = {…: 0}` and only `+= 1` in `_ensure_processes_alive`, with no reset when a process becomes healthy again), so intermittent hangs over long runtimes can eventually exceed `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` and raise `RuntimeError`, taking down the consumer. Additionally, on restart it only attempts to kill if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`; when `produce_to_pipe` is set (threading mode), a hung thread is never stopped/killed before starting a replacement in `_create_process_for_shards`, which can leak/accumulate stuck threads. Both behaviors are directly shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:51 — --flusher-processes` is not validated: 0 (or None from the factory default) silently falls back to one spawned process per shard, each with its own Sentry/Django init, KafkaProducer and Redis clients, while a negative value gives `num_processes<0`, an empty map and a KeyError at line 66 during strategy creation

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` makes `--flusher-processes 0` (falsy) silently behave as “per-shard” instead of respecting the provided value. Worse, a negative value is truthy, so `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative; `range(self.num_processes)` yields an empty `process_to_shards_map`, and the subsequent shard assignment does `process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` with `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, which will produce a key (e.g. 0) that is not present, causing a runtime failure (KeyError) during initialization. The new click option uses `type=int` with no bounds, so negative values are permitted by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:300 — The memory check and record_stored_segments now loop over every per-process SpansBuffer on the consumer's submit path, so cluster-wide memory INFO queries (and the used/available sums) are repeated N times against the same Redis nodes; the ratio stays the same, but Redis round-trips in the hot consumer thread grow linearly with N

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the code now iterates `for buffer in self.buffers.values()` and aggregates `buffer.get_memory_info()` and calls `buffer.record_stored_segments()`. But each entry in `self.buffers` is a per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` created with a disjoint subset of `buffer.assigned_shards` (see `_create_process_for_shards` and the modulo distribution into `process_to_shards_map`). From the diff alone, this does not imply “cluster-wide INFO queries are repeated N times against the same Redis nodes”; it more directly implies the work is partitioned by shard and then summed, which could be equivalent to the prior single-buffer call. The claim about duplicated Redis round-trips depends on `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` implementation, which is not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — No test covers _ensure_processes_alive restarts, hiding a regression: SpawnProcess is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process (verified), so hung/dead spawn processes are never killed before a replacement is started, leaving duplicate flushers on the same shards

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, on hang detection it conditionally kills the old worker only if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` (new code around the restart logic). But workers are created via `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `make_process = self.mp_context.Process`, i.e. they are spawn-context process objects. If that `isinstance` check does not match spawn-context processes, the hung process will not be killed/terminated and `_create_process_for_shards(...)` will start a replacement anyway, potentially leaving duplicate flushers handling the same shard set. The diff adds no test that exercises the restart/kill path of `_ensure_processes_alive`, so this regression would be unobserved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:115 — test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts the structure (process count, echoed max_processes, total shard count); it never submits spans or checks that shared processes flush segments from every shard, and it doesn't check the actual shard-to-process distribution or the per-process buffers

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the assertions only check metadata/structure (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `flusher.max_processes == 2`, `flusher.num_processes == 2`, and that the sum of shard-list lengths equals 4). The test never drives the system by submitting messages/spans, never verifies that flushing/producing occurs for shards handled by a shared process, and does not assert the actual shard-to-process mapping contents (only the total) nor that per-process `SpansBuffer` instances in `flusher.buffers` correspond to the expected shard groups. Given the new nontrivial sharding-to-process logic in `SpanFlusher.__init__` / `_create_process_for_shards`, this is a specific coverage gap rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:247 — Per-process hang detection (process_healthy_since), per-process process_restarts, and the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError have no tests, and restarts are now counted per process, so the consumer tolerates up to N*11 restarts before crashing

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes restart accounting from a single counter to a per-process dict (`self.process_restarts = {process_index: 0 ...}`) and enforces the threshold per process (`if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS: raise ...`), so total tolerated restarts can scale with the number of flusher processes. The added tests only cover process limiting/shard distribution and backpressure (`test_flusher_processes_limit`, `assert any(...)`), and do not exercise per-process hang detection via `process_healthy_since` nor the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError path in `_ensure_processes_alive()`. This is a specific, diff-grounded testing gap and behavioral change, not a directly provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — join() with several processes and a deadline is untested: once the deadline passes, the loop breaks and skips terminate() for the remaining processes

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` breaks when `deadline` has passed (`if remaining_time <= 0: break`), which prevents calling `process.terminate()` for any remaining processes not yet iterated. Since `terminate()` is the only forced shutdown for `multiprocessing.Process` instances here, those later processes can be left running beyond the timeout. The diff adds multi-process support and this shutdown path; the new tests do not cover `join(timeout=...)` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:278 — No test checks that backpressure from one of several processes makes submit() raise MessageRejected; test_flusher.py:83 switched to any() but still uses one shard, so the multi-process path is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes SpanFlusher from a single process to multiple processes and updates backpressure handling in submit() to iterate over self.process_backpressure_since.values() and raise MessageRejected if any process has exceeded the backpressure window. The only modified assertion in tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py switches to `any(...)`, but nothing in this diff shows a test that exercises the multi-process case where one of several processes enters backpressure and submit() rejects. The newly added test_flusher_processes_limit only checks process/shard distribution, not backpressure behavior. This is a specific missing-test gap for newly added nontrivial logic rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:62 — The added time.sleep(0.1) does nothing because line 15 monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op on the same module, so the "give flusher threads time" comment is misleading and any race it was meant to cover is still there

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` replaces `time.sleep` globally in the `time` module. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` therefore also becomes a no-op, so it cannot “give flusher threads time to process” as the comment claims. If the sleep was intended to reduce a race/flakiness, this change is ineffective and leaves the race unaddressed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:12 — django_db(transaction=True) was added to both tests with no stated reason (test_flusher.py runs the same threaded flusher with no DB mark), and transactional tests truncate tables on teardown, which slows the suite

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `test_basic` from `@pytest.mark.django_db` to `@pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True)` and adds the same transactional mark to the newly added `test_flusher_processes_limit` (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py). The diff does not show any new database-transaction-specific behavior in these tests that would clearly require `transaction=True` (they primarily exercise the consumer/flusher logic and use `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, which selects the threaded flusher path). Making tests transactional is a concrete, suite-performance concern and should be justified or avoided if unnecessary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:433 — The new --flusher-processes CLI option and its wiring into the factory have no tests, and its default (1) differs from the factory/SpanFlusher default (None = one per shard), so tests only run a default path that production doesn't use (and only with a single shard)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new Click option `--flusher-processes` with `default=1` in `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py`, while `SpanFlusher` defaults to `max_processes=None` which becomes `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (one per shard) in `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`. This is a real behavioral divergence for the default CLI path vs the class default and is worth clarifying/testing. However, the finding’s claim that there are no tests / only single-shard coverage is not fully accurate: `test_flusher_processes_limit` (new) exercises `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(... flusher_processes=2)` and multiple shards (4 partitions), though it does not test Click parsing/wiring of the CLI default itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:51 — Edge cases have no validation or tests: flusher_processes=0 silently means one per shard, a negative value causes a KeyError at startup (range(-1) gives an empty map but i % -1 == 0), and flusher_processes > shards is not exercised

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as falsy (silently converting `flusher_processes=0` into “one per shard”), and a negative `max_processes` leads to `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` being negative. That makes `range(self.num_processes)` empty when building `process_to_shards_map`, but the subsequent loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and then indexes `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]`, which will raise (empty map / invalid configuration). The diff adds the CLI option as `type=int` with no validation, so this crash is reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:300 — Aggregating Redis memory across multiple per-process buffers is untested; if get_memory_info reports the whole cluster, each node is counted N times (SpansBuffer source isn't in this snapshot, so this is unverified)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `submit()` to aggregate memory info across multiple per-process buffers: `memory_infos = []` then `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())` (around flusher.py:296). This new behavior could double-count if `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` reports cluster/global memory rather than per-shard/per-buffer memory, but that cannot be verified from this diff because `SpansBuffer` implementation isn’t shown. It is a concrete, diff-grounded risk introduced by the change and appears untested in the added tests (which cover process limits/backpressure, not memory aggregation).
